objective: Configure synchronization in Argo CD: manual and automated sync, prune and self-heal, sync waves and hooks, sync options, and reading diffs
secondaryObjectives: Troubleshoot common reconciliation patterns: OutOfSync caused by drift, ignoring differences, resource hooks, degraded health, and a sync that fails

sources.cite: Linux Foundation, Certified Argo Project Associate (CAPA) exam page: Argo Workflows 36%, Argo CD 34%, Argo Rollouts 18%, Argo Events 12%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of the Linux Foundation's page (last modified 2026-05-06). Its Argo Workflows topics are workflow fundamentals, artifacts, templates, the workflow spec, DAGs ('Work with DAG (Directed-Acyclic Graphs)') and data processing jobs; it does not mention retries or exit handlers. A study page (kube-dojo.github.io/k8s/capa, same weights) lists retryStrategy, backoff and exit handlers as study topics. The objective wording is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's argo-nightly-dag-region-failure (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of the page found by search. Prune=false on a resource stops it being pruned (the app shows OutOfSync); Replace=true uses kubectl replace or create and 'has the potential to be destructive'; PruneLast prunes in a final wave after the rest is healthy; a resource's Prune sync option overrides the Application's prune policy.

sources.cite: Argo CD documentation, Sync Phases and Waves; Automated Sync Policy (prune, selfHeal, ignoreDifferences)
sources.note: Found by search 2026-11-17 (argo-cd.readthedocs.io user guide); read only through search results, to verify against the pages. PreSync hooks run before the application's manifests are applied; sync-wave annotations order resources within a phase; selfHeal re-applies Git when the live state drifts; ignoreDifferences excludes fields such as /spec/replicas from the diff.
The company, the cluster, the applications and the people are fictional. The minutes each check-in takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice.

brief.situation: You are the on-call platform engineer at Harborline Freight, a fictional logistics company. Its orders service is deployed by Argo CD from the platform Git repository with automated sync, prune and self-heal on. This morning a developer merged a refactor that moved the orders database's StatefulSet and PersistentVolumeClaim from apps/orders/ into a new apps/orders-db/ application that has not synced yet.
handover: The orders Application: automated sync with prune: true and selfHeal: true, target revision main.
The refactor's pull request was approved for the code change; nobody reviewed the diff Argo CD will apply.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: the orders app is still OutOfSync; two other fixes wait behind it.
Check-in 2: the orders database is gone; its volume was deleted with the claim. Orders fail until a restore from last night's backup.
Check-in 3: Pods start and terminate every few seconds; a third of orders time out during the spike.
Check-in 4: the replaced Deployment has no serving Pods; orders are down until the migration is run.

else.log: The refactor is live and the on-call window ends.

effects.log: Check-in 1: the next automated sync is minutes away.
Check-in 2: a traffic spike, and the on-call developer scaled orders-api by hand.
Check-in 3: the new orders-api Pods crash on start.

prunePrompt.title: 14 resources would be pruned, the database among them
prunePrompt.context: Argo CD will sync the orders app on its next poll. The diff prunes the database StatefulSet and its volume claim, which belong to the new orders-db app now. The reclaim policy is Delete, so the volume would go with the claim.

choices.label: Pause automated sync on the orders app, annotate the StatefulSet and claim with argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false, sync orders-db so it adopts them, then turn automation back on

effects.log: Automation paused; the database resources carry Prune=false; orders-db adopts them.

choices.feedback: Reading the diff and protecting the resources with a sync option stops the prune; the new app adopts them before automation resumes.

choices.label: Turn automated sync off for orders and leave it OutOfSync until someone can look at it next week

effects.log: Automated sync off; orders stays OutOfSync.

choices.feedback: Safe, but the app drifts for a week and nobody adopts the database: the next person to press Sync with prune hits the same trap.

choices.label: Let the automated sync run: Git is the source of truth

effects.output: argocd: sync orders: pruned apps/StatefulSet orders/orders-db, PersistentVolumeClaim orders/data-orders-db-0 (12 more)

choices.feedback: Git is the source of truth, but a prune applies whatever the diff says; nobody read it, and the database left with the path.

healPrompt.title: Self-heal keeps undoing the emergency scale-up
healPrompt.context: Orders traffic tripled. The developer ran kubectl scale to 12 replicas; self-heal put it back to 4 within seconds, twice. Git says replicas: 4, and an autoscaler is planned for next sprint.

choices.label: Change replicas to 12 in Git through a fast-tracked pull request and let Argo CD sync it; note ignoreDifferences on /spec/replicas for when the autoscaler owns the field

effects.log: The pull request merges; Argo CD syncs 12 replicas and keeps them.

choices.feedback: With self-heal on, the change belongs in desired state. When an autoscaler owns replicas, ignoreDifferences keeps Argo CD from fighting it.

choices.label: Turn self-heal off for the orders app so the manual scale sticks

effects.log: Self-heal off; the 12 replicas stay, Git still says 4.

choices.feedback: It works today, but the live state now differs from Git silently, and the next sync puts it back to 4.

choices.label: Put kubectl scale in a loop every 10 seconds until traffic drops

effects.log: The loop and self-heal fight over the replica count.

choices.feedback: Fighting the reconciler makes Pods start and stop every few seconds; orders time out while they flap.

hookPrompt.title: The new release needs its schema migration first
hookPrompt.context: The release adds a column. Argo CD applies the migration Job and the new Deployment in the same wave, so new Pods start before the column exists and crash; old Pods still serve.

choices.label: Make the migration a PreSync hook (argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync, hook-delete-policy BeforeHookCreation) so it completes before the Deployment is applied, and sync

effects.log: The PreSync migration runs, then the Deployment rolls out cleanly.

choices.feedback: A PreSync hook (or an earlier sync wave) makes the order part of desired state, for every future sync.

choices.label: Run the migration by hand with kubectl, then press Sync again

effects.log: You run the Job by hand; the next sync rolls out.

choices.feedback: It gets today's release out, but the order lives in your head: the next release with a migration crashes the same way.

choices.label: Force a sync with Replace=true so everything is recreated together

effects.log: Argo CD replaces the resources; the old Pods go too.

choices.feedback: Replace does not order anything; it recreated the Deployment, so the old Pods that were still serving went too.

reflection.question: Write the change record for the platform team: what the diff showed and how the prune was handled, and how the scale-up and the migration were made part of desired state.

parts.label: The prune
parts.criteria: Names the 14 pruned resources, the database among them, and how Prune=false and the new app's adoption kept it, with automation paused while it happened.
parts.modelAnswer: The diff pruned the orders database's StatefulSet and claim because they moved to orders-db. We paused automation, annotated them Prune=false, let orders-db adopt them and resumed.

parts.label: Desired state
parts.criteria: The scale-up went through Git (with ignoreDifferences for a future autoscaler) and the migration became a PreSync hook, instead of fighting self-heal or forcing a replace.
parts.modelAnswer: Self-heal reverted the manual scale, so we changed replicas in Git. The migration now runs as a PreSync hook, so new Pods never start before the column exists.

expertPath.text: Read the diff before the next automated sync, and the application's sync policy.
Pause automation, protect the database with Prune=false, sync orders-db to adopt it, then resume.
Make the scale-up a Git change, and plan ignoreDifferences for the autoscaler.
Make the migration a PreSync hook so it runs before the Deployment on every sync.

pruneHarm.headline: A prune applies the diff, read or not
pruneHarm.body: Automated sync with prune deletes whatever left the path. Read the diff; protect stateful resources with Prune=false while another app adopts them.

healHarm.headline: Never fight the reconciler
healHarm.body: With self-heal on, change desired state. A manual change is reverted; a loop against it makes things worse.

hookHarm.headline: Replace is not ordering
hookHarm.body: Replace=true can be destructive. Order the migration with a PreSync hook or a sync wave.

target.headline: Good: synced safely, every change in desired state
target.body: The diff was read and the prune stopped, the scale-up went through Git, and the migration was ordered by a hook.

partly.headline: Done, with gaps
partly.body: Nothing was harmed, but a decision was only partly right, or the record left something out. The criteria say which.

scoring.modelReasoning: Automated sync with prune applies whatever the diff says: resources that leave an app's path are deleted, and with a Delete reclaim policy the data goes with the claim. Read the diff, pause automation, protect stateful resources with the Prune=false sync option and let the new application adopt them. With self-heal on, a manual change is reverted, so the scale-up belongs in Git, and a field an autoscaler owns belongs in ignoreDifferences. Ordering is part of desired state too: a PreSync hook or an earlier sync wave runs the migration before the Deployment; Replace=true orders nothing and can be destructive.
